findings.title: type: strategy frontmatter is a silent hard requirement for a dropped-in strategy, but AC-N1 / T-DROP only say 'valid frontmatter'
findings.problem: registry.strategies() filters m.type == 'strategy'. A dropped-in strategies/<new>.md that omits type: strategy is discovered by discover() but silently excluded from strategy_names(), so the planner never sees it. AC-N1/T-DROP say only 'valid frontmatter'.
findings.fix: Make AC-N1 and T-DROP require the fixture's strategies/<new>.md to carry name: <new> and type: strategy (mirroring strategies/balanced.md), and add a T-DROP sentence noting registry.strategies() requires type: strategy.

findings.title: 'built once / not recomposed per tick' not fully proven by T-STATIC
findings.problem: T-STATIC proves the base is not rebuilt, but does not guard against a future refactor calling build_static_base() inside compose_tick_prompt per tick.
findings.fix: In T-STATIC add a call-counter spy on build_static_base; after register, run N ticks and assert the counter stays at 1.

findings.title: limits={'turns':2} enforcement relied upon but not re-verified against installed Strands 1.13.0
findings.problem: Only a fake agent honors the turns cap in tests; real-library enforcement is unverified. The whole anti-loop guarantee for the real runtime rests on this assumption (design flags it honestly).
findings.fix: In AC-A3 name the 3.5s asyncio.wait_for wall-clock timeout as the authoritative loop bound and limits={'turns':2} as best-effort with unverified real-library enforcement.

findings.title: effective_pid = my_players[0] can misroute when myPlayers is present but lacks this agent's own id
findings.problem: my_players[0] blindly trusts the payload. A full-roster myPlayers would make every agent resolve to id 0 (GK) and load gk/<strategy>.md. T-ROUTE's myPlayers=[pid] cases would not catch it.
findings.fix: Either document in AC-B3 that myPlayers is contractually a single-element list [thisAgentId] (and T-ROUTE need not cover multi-element lists), or harden resolution to prefer the pinned my_player_id when present in the list and add a T-ROUTE case with myPlayers=[0,1,2,3,4].

findings.title: optional skill-body softening edits have no guard keeping bodies non-load-bearing
findings.problem: §11 lists optional per-body edits; nothing stops a future contributor from relying on them and regressing AC-N3. T-TOOL enforces this only implicitly via a tool-free body.
findings.fix: State explicitly in AC-N3 that no skill body may be the sole source of decide-with-facts (T-TOOL enforces with a zero-tool-mention body); optionally drop the §11 body edits to keep the change surface to tool_catalog.md + two Python modules + docs + tests.
